task: nivo expert academy public landing and student auth
parityBaseline: nivo/apps/expert/src/components/blocks/landing/LandingPage.tsx (landing only; the student auth page has no legacy render)
sharedDecisions: Each academy runs as its own provisioned instance, so the template is MOUNTED AS A FILE at provision time rather than fetched per request. There is no tenant lookup, no per-request brand query, and no unstyled first paint.

Colour reaches the screen only through CSS variables written on the root by one owner. A component naming a shade looks right for the academy it was written beside and wrong for every other, so the brand read is confined to AcademyChrome.
The auth page serves STUDENTS. The expert administers from the nivo control plane where they are already signed in.
Section order is data: array position IS render order, and a section switched off leaves no hole.
An unrecognised system key is skipped silently so an older build survives a newer catalog; an expert-authored section carries its own content and therefore cannot be swallowed by that path.
Images are links the expert pastes. nivo stores no file, so 'no link yet' and 'link has died' are ordinary states, not edge cases.
An already-authenticated student is sent to the academy dashboard. The route is not built in this batch, so the auth page owns the redirect and nothing renders a destination that does not exist.

unknowns: U-A: is an external image request from a student's browser to a third-party host acceptable? `no-referrer` is set but the student's address is still exposed.
U-B: `stats`, `testimonials` and instructor credentials are unverifiable claims served from nivo's infrastructure. Same family as BR-B07 but a different mechanism, and no rule covers it.
U-C: is `instructor` a system section or a custom one? Every academy needs it, but its content belongs to one person. It is the first case BR-B06's two families do not cut cleanly.
U-D: does an academy run on its own domain or a nivo subdomain? This decides how dangerous a deceptive section is.
U-E: three rungs the model predicts and no reference academy has - guarantee, audience, schedule. Not yet built.

U-F RESOLVED (user, 2026-08-12): an already-authenticated student is redirected to the academy dashboard. That route does not exist yet and is a separate later work item, so this batch renders the redirect intent and never a dashboard it cannot prove.

businessCapabilities.capability: named colour slots to CSS variables

preliminaryDirections.name: Ladder, in catalog order
preliminaryDirections.thesis: A stranger climbs one rung at a time in the order the catalog already names, and every rung can be switched off without the page losing its footing.
preliminaryDirections.primaryCta: Landing: start the free trial. Auth: create an account.
tradeoffs: Matches the catalog exactly, so nothing has to be explained to the backend.
Longest page; a reader who came to see the price scrolls furthest.
Least opinionated, which is also the weakest claim to being designed.
legacyDivergence: Reordering is newly exposed; the legacy render treated order as fixed.

preliminaryDirections.name: Proof before offer
preliminaryDirections.thesis: Nobody buys a course from a stranger, so who is teaching and who already finished come BEFORE what it costs, and the auth page puts the instructor beside the form so a student sees whose academy they are joining.
preliminaryDirections.primaryCta: Landing: start the free trial. Auth: create an account, with the instructor visible.
tradeoffs: Leads with the rung all three reference academies lean hardest on.
An academy with no instructor photo, no testimonials and no figures - every academy on day one - collapses to almost nothing.
Concentrates unverifiable claims at the top of the page, which is exactly where U-B bites hardest.
legacyDivergence: Credibility promoted above the offer; the legacy render put courses first.

preliminaryDirections.name: One question at a time
preliminaryDirections.thesis: The page asks for a decision as early as it honestly can: a short funnel of hero, outcomes, courses and capture, with every other rung folded behind one disclosure - and the auth page asks for an email before it asks for anything else.
preliminaryDirections.primaryCta: Landing: leave your contact. Auth: continue with your email.
tradeoffs: Shortest path to a lead, which is the site's proven business job.
Folding rungs away hides exactly the proof a cautious buyer needs; the fold becomes the whole design decision.
Splitting auth into email-then-password adds a step for returning students and needs a backend check that does not exist.
legacyDivergence: Disclosure is new; the legacy render showed every enabled section inline.

recommendationEvidence: The catalog and its order are already settled by the backend and confirmed by all three reference academies, so L-A is the only direction that needs no unproven claim. L-B collapses on a new academy, which is every academy on day one. L-C's email-first auth step needs a backend account-existence check, and that check is precisely what the password-reset e2e proves the product refuses to expose.

contracts.why: The sections are peers in one column rather than nested, so switching one off removes a row instead of leaving a hole, and moving one changes only its position.

vocabularyProposals.name: AcademyChrome
vocabularyProposals.reasonForDecision: It is the single reader of the mounted template and the single writer of the palette. Any block reading the brand directly reproduces the failure BR-B02 forbids.
vocabularyProposals.reasonAlternativesFail: A hook every block could call spreads one decision across every block and leaves nowhere to prove theming works.

vocabularyProposals.name: StudentEntryPanel
vocabularyProposals.reasonForDecision: The control plane's SignInPanel is weighted for someone who already has an account. A student's entry leads with registration, which is a different product sentence rather than a variant.
vocabularyProposals.reasonAlternativesFail: Adding a mode flag to SignInPanel would make one block answer two different questions depending on a boolean.

backendEnablerProposals.uiNeed: L-C only: decide whether to ask for a password after an email is entered.
backendEnablerProposals.currentEvidence: The password-reset e2e proves the product deliberately refuses to disclose whether an email has an account.
rejectedAlternatives: Inferring existence from a sign-in attempt, which discloses the same fact more slowly.
backendEnablerProposals.escalationTrigger: Already escalated: it contradicts an existing, tested privacy decision. This is the reason L-C's auth half cannot ship as described.
